scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

F-01.statement: Disputed bills by read type: ESTIMATED=1240, ACTUAL=1785

F-02.statement: Route completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 (target 0.95) with 9,200 manual read accounts.

F-05.statement: Dispute ticket median response time is 1.6 days (p90 2.8 days, SLA 3 days, total tickets 2440)

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAME.statement: The requester frames the problem as incorrect bills leading to doubled dispute tickets, proposing an AI agent to auto-answer and fix bills.

H-AMI-READ-ISSUE.statement: Delayed or missing AMI reads in the MDMS cause estimation substitution, producing incorrect bills and disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-ISSUE.statement: Missed or delayed contracted field manual reads due to route changes or staffing gaps lead to estimation and wrong bills.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced calculation errors, resulting in wrong bills and a dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows more disputed bills have ACTUAL reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240), indicating that disputes are not solely driven by estimation substitution.
Field route completion for August‑September 2026 is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating that manual meter reads are being missed or delayed.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating no recent tariff changes were logged in the billing database.
The observation shows dispute ticket volume rose from ~610 in June to 1260 in September 2026, indicating a sharp increase during August‑September.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.
The observation shows that dispute tickets have a median response time of 1.6 days, well within the 3‑day SLA, indicating that response speed is not a primary driver of the dispute surge.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder states there has been no tariff change this year, suggesting tariff changes are not driving the dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract shows that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager, indicating a control mechanism for route changes. This observation does not address billing calculation errors or the root cause of the dispute surge.

U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S.question: Which specific validation rule(s) introduced the calculation error?
U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S.decision_impact: Without identifying the faulty rule(s) a fix cannot be applied.
U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S.resolution_path: Inspect billing-config change logs for August‑September, run test bills with known reads to isolate the erroneous rule.
U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S.safe_placeholder: Continue monitoring dispute volume and manually review a statistically significant sample of bills under K-BILLWRITE authority.

U-SCOPE-OF-IMPACT.question: Does the rule change affect all bill types or only certain customer segments?
U-SCOPE-OF-IMPACT.decision_impact: If limited to a segment, a targeted fix may suffice; otherwise a system‑wide change is needed.
U-SCOPE-OF-IMPACT.resolution_path: Segment dispute tickets by account type or tariff and compare bill calculations for each segment.
U-SCOPE-OF-IMPACT.safe_placeholder: Apply manual bill adjustments for high‑value disputes pending clarification, respecting K-BILLWRITE.

U-MANUAL-READ-HANDOFF-QUALITY.question: Are there concurrent data quality issues in the field‑to‑billing manual read handoff that could compound errors?
U-MANUAL-READ-HANDOFF-QUALITY.decision_impact: If handoff errors exist, they must be addressed alongside rule fixes.
U-MANUAL-READ-HANDOFF-QUALITY.resolution_path: Audit route completion logs (route-log) and manual read upload logs (H-FIELD-BILL) for missing or corrupted reads.
U-MANUAL-READ-HANDOFF-QUALITY.safe_placeholder: Rely on existing SLA monitoring for route completion and manual read timeliness.

A-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.statement: The rule change occurred recently enough to explain the August‑September dispute surge.

A-CALCULATION-ERROR-IMPACT.statement: Calculation errors in the import rules affect bill amounts sufficiently to generate disputes.

A-ABSENCE-OF-OTHER-DRIVERS.statement: Other factors such as customer behavior or external tariff changes are not primary drivers of the dispute increase.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

K-DISPATCH.description: Changes to field dispatch routes are executed only after runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (service contract §4.2).

K-BILLWRITE.description: Writes to customer bills (re-bill, credit) require Billing Operations authority; no automated bill writes.

SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE.statement: Monthly dispute ticket volume returns to pre‑August baseline of ≤610 tickets.
SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE.validation_method: Query crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly for the most recent month and compare count to 610.

problem_definition.root_problem: Incorrect bill calculations due to recent changes to billing import validation rules cause wrong bills (even with actual meter reads) and drive the observed increase in dispute tickets.

trace.summary: Incorrect bill calculations due to recent changes to billing import validation rules cause wrong bills (even with actual meter reads) and drive the observed increase in dispute tickets.

structural_remedies.description: Revert the problematic billing import validation rule change and implement a controlled change‑management process with pre‑deployment validation using test bills.
structural_remedies.rationale: Rule change is a configuration edit; estimated effort <30 minutes, well within the 225 minutes remaining. It does not involve automated bill writes (K‑BILLWRITE) and can be performed by Billing Operations (SH‑BILL) under existing authority.; residual gap: After fixing the rule, most disputes from incorrect bills should cease. A small residual dispute volume may remain due to field staffing shortages causing estimated bills for a minority of customers (<5 % of current volume).

solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: If the specific faulty validation rule(s) (U-EXACT-FAULTY-RULE-S) cannot be identified within the remaining budget, apply a temporary manual bill review process as a bridge until identification.
